newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL palm oil higher at close ahead of PORLA.
newsitem.headline: KL palm oil higher at close ahead of PORLA.

text.p: PALM OIL FUTURES PALM OIL PHYSICAL
May (3rd pos) 1,250 rgt/tonne Mar (south) 1,287.50*
Open/Hi/Low 1,244/1,252/1,238 Prev close 1,285
Prev settlement 1,244 * sellers prices

PALM OIL FUTURES - Prices closed mostly higher on late shortcovering ahead of official PORLA crop report for February on Saturday. The market drifted narrowly in earlier trade amid market uncertainty following lower soyoil prices. May futures' resistance - 1,260/support - 1,240.
PALM OIL PHYSICAL - Lack of demand limited activity with a neutral crop report from Ivan Wong having no impact on prices.
The Palm oil Registration and Licensing Authority (PORLA) is scheduled to release its February stock/output/export crop data at 0430 GMT on Saturday.

"If PORLA comes out with supportive data, we will see the market trying to test the next resistance of 1,260 and then 1,280 on Monday," a chartist. "But if the data is bearish then the contract may trade at 1,240 and then 1,230."
The May futures contract closed six ringgit higher at 1,250 ringgit ($504.64) a tonne after trading between 1,238 and 1,252 on Friday.
A crop report from private forecaster Ivan Wong had no impact on the market as the figures were within market expectations and little changed from his previous projections.
Malaysia's palm oil output in February is expected to fall by 11.8 percent to 509,000 tonnes from January, Wong said on Friday.
He had previously projected falls of 21 and 13 percent.
Wong put palm oil stocks at the end of February at 675,000 tonnes, compared with PORLA's 696,272 tonnes at end-January.
"People were very nervous. They are seen liquidating their positions at the highs while some bargain hunting activity was seen at lower levels in earlier trade," a trader said.
Lower soyoil prices in Chicago overnight also dampened sentiment this morning, traders said, adding that players also speculated further drop in soyoil after recent volatility.

Among physicals, March (south) crude palm ol was offered at 1,287.50 ringgit against bids of 1,285 after trading from 1,280 to 1,285. March (central) saw offers at 1,275 against bids of 1,265 and March (north) at 1,260 against 1,250.
Apr (south) was offered at 1,285 with bids at 1,277.50 with early transactions at 1,275 and 1,277.50, and Apr (central) at 1,275 against 1,260.
Among refined products, Mar RBD palm oil was offered at $552.50 a tonne FOB Malaysia, Apr at $545, May at $540 and June at $537.50.
Mar RBD palm olein saw offers at $585, Apr at $580 and May/Jun at $572.50. Apr was dealt at $575 and May at $569.
Mar RBD palm stearin was offered at $452.50 and Mar/Apr palm fatty acid distillate saw sellers at $310.
